# IFC Startup Catalyst
To help close this gap, in 2016 IFC launched Startup Catalyst - a platform designed to invest in accelerators and pre-seed, seed, and pre-Series A funds supporting innovative early-stage startups. In addition to investment capital, IFC Startup Catalyst provides funds and accelerators with access to networks, training, and sector expertise.

## Results (as of FY26)
- $111 millionInvested in Funds
- 760+Startups in 53 emerging markets
- 40,000+Jobs supported
- 30accelerators and early-stage funds

## Startup Catalyst by Region
### Africa
[![Logo: Catalyst Fund](https://s7d1.scene7.com/is/image/wbcollab/logo-catalyst-fund?qlt=90&fmt=webp)](https://www.antler.co/location/kenya)

IFC invested in Catalyst Fund Resilience I, L.P. (“Catalyst Fund”) in 2026. [Catalyst Fund](https://www.thecatalystfund.com/) is a pan-African pre-seed fund that invests in startups building climate adaptation and resilience solutions across Africa.

IFC invested in Pamoja Ventures, LP (“P1 Ventures”) in 2024.  [P1 Ventures](https://www.p1.ventures/) is a Nigeria-based early-stage venture capital fund with a pan-Africa mandate, that invests in artificial intelligence, machine learning, e-commerce, fintech, healthtech, insurtech, and SaaS sectors.

web.description:
# African startups that raised funding in September 2026
## AirSmat
**Funding raised in Sep 2026:** [$150k from Village Capital’s Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility](https://african-startups.com/countries/nigeria/village-capital-expands-into-nigeria-with-450k-first-investments-in-trade-lenda-and-airsmat/)

AirSmat is a Nigerian climate technology company.

## Drive45 Mobility
Drive45 is a Lagos-based mobility company providing transport solutions to businesses across Nigeria.

## PowerGen Renewable Energy Nigeria Limited
**Founded year:** 2011

**CEO:** [Aaron Cheng](https://ke.linkedin.com/in/aaroncheng)

**Funding raised in Sep 2026:** [$5 million mezzanine facility from All On](https://african-startups.com/countries/nigeria/all-on-invests-5-million-in-powergen-to-expand-solar-mini-grids-across-nigeria/)

PowerGen is a developer of solar mini-grid and off-grid power infrastructure. It delivers commercial, industrial and off-grid solar energy solutions. The company has installed more than 325 renewable energy systems, representing roughly 34 MW+MWh of solar photovoltaic and battery storage capacity, across 12 countries, with operating teams in Nigeria, Kenya, Sierra Leone and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

## Bekia
**Funding raised in Sep 2026:** [$765k Seed round led by Madica](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/egypts-bekia-raises-765k-to-digitise-waste-collection-and-launch-its-first-b2b-software-product/),

It has diverted more than 25,000 tonnes of waste from landfill.

## Tomato Jos
It is a vertically integrated tomato paste maker described by Sabou as having Nigeria’s most technologically advanced tomato processing facility.

## Talenteo
**Funding raised in Sep 2026:** Up to $200k from Madica

## Paysika
**Funding raised in Sep 2026:** Up to $200k from Madica

## Nomba
**CEO:** [Yinka Adewale](https://ng.linkedin.com/in/yinka-adewale-7b779448)

Nomba is a Nigerian FinTech company that provides payment processing and banking services for businesses. Nomba currently handles over $480 million in cross-border payments monthly and aims to raise $20 million to $50 million in debt, with a goal of reaching $1 billion in monthly payments.
